prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: FAA NextGen raises National Airspace System (NAS) capacity; en route weather causes ~70% of US delays. System: NASA ATD-3 decision aids. Subset: NASA Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR), cruise phase, extends NASA Direct-To; constraints are polygons. Current: FAA traffic managers set static Flow Constrained Areas (FCA) and Severe Weather Avoidance Plans (SWAP, aka Playbook routes) 2-8 h ahead; airline dispatchers file plans >=45 min before push-back; CTOP strategic only; amendments manual. DWR: ground automation analyzing aircraft at/above 10,000 ft from radar track and flight plan updates; seeks time/fuel-saving weather-avoidance or wind-favorable corrections considering convective weather, traffic conflicts, sector congestion, Special Use Airspace (SUA), FAA restrictions. Route from Maneuver Start Point (MSP; default 5 min ahead or FL240 entry in Fort Worth Center, ZFW; draggable; snaps to fix within 10 nmi) to Return Capture Fix (RCF; last fix in ZFW ~200 nmi rectangle or before STAR). Alternative: historical limit polygon in NASCENT (FACET version of DWR). If savings >= user minimum (default 5 min), route probed; 1-2 auxiliary waypoints; conflicted trial plans dismissed. Advisories go to DWR flight list on FAA traffic manager's or airline ATC coordinator's display, sorted by savings; fields: flight ID, savings, city pair, aircraft type, RCF, waypoint count, TR (min to traffic conflict), SC, WX, 'R' (Route TMI). GUI: advisory dashed-white; capture fix menu with savings; sector congestion red=airborne, yellow=incl. proposed departures. Research: datalink of DWR routes ATC-flight deck plus on-board display speeds approval. Weather model: DWR receives forecasts from FAA Corridor Integrated Weather System (CIWS; growth/decay/movement, updates every 5 min, 2-h look-ahead in 5-min steps) and Convective Weather Avoidance Model (CWAM), which produces Weather Avoidance Field (WAF) polygons (60/70/80% probability of pilot deviation, based on intensity, echo tops, look-ahead; higher % = smaller) per 5-min interval to 2 h, FL250-FL450 per 1,000 ft. DWR uses 70% WAF by

New part:
U0126: This function includes a distance buffer that will reject a route amendment if it will go through a gap that is narrower than 50nm laterally (user-adjustable parameter) either side of route and 75nm longitudinally (user-adjustable parameter) to the predicted cells at the time the aircraft reaches the point closest to the cells (see Figure 9).
U0127: If convective cells are predicted to encroach on one side of a trajectory but not on the other, (blue polygons in left graphic of Figure 9) it is generally not considered an operational problem because there is room for flight crews to maneuver around the cell.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
